author: EmuCore - Hub
title: I Built A PS2 Portable - The PS2 Eclipse
summary: GingerOfOz builds the PS2 Eclipse handheld from a physically trimmed PS2 motherboard. The video shows its construction, working games and remaining limitations.

blocks.text: The roughly twelve-minute build story follows a failed first motherboard trim, a successful replacement, enclosure design and the custom electronics needed for controls, audio, storage and power. Finished-system footage demonstrates several games and shows the ports and physical layout. The project uses original PS2 hardware for PS2 games rather than emulating the console on a phone. The video includes a disclosed PCBWay sponsorship.

The author also shows limitations: USB loading can produce long waits and uneven cutscenes, some games fail to recognize the controller, and battery life is described as around two and a half hours for this build. Those caveats are more informative than a blanket compatibility claim. This is a project retrospective, not a safe step-by-step electronics tutorial or a product currently offered for sale. Cutting a motherboard and building a battery-powered device require skills beyond following a short montage.
